attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-09-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Rodriguez, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Fell from monkey bars landing on outstretched right hand with severe arm pain and refusal to move right arm

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
Eight months after a prior fall from a tree, he landed on his outstretched right hand and now refuses to use his right arm due to severe pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Non-displaced supracondylar fracture of humerus (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

MEDICATIONS:
He takes no medications.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Negative for bleeding disorders
- Negative for bone fragility syndromes
- No family history of developmental dysplasia

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the right arm is held in slight flexion and pronation, with prominent swelling and tenderness just above the elbow. There is a noticeable deformity with the distal arm appearing posteriorly displaced. The radial pulse is weak compared to the left arm, and the boy reports numbness in his thumb, index, and middle fingers. Capillary refill in the right hand is delayed.

IMAGING:
An X-ray of the right arm reveals a supracondylar fracture with posterior displacement of the distal humerus fragment.
